title: Echocardiogram (heart ultrasound)
what: An ultrasound that shows your heart moving: how the chambers and valves work, and how strongly your heart pumps.
why: For heart murmurs, shortness of breath, swelling, high blood pressure, and before surgery or sports.
tell_doctor: What medicines you take for your heart or blood pressure
If you have had heart surgery or have valve implants

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable. You will undress to the waist. Women should avoid a one-piece bodysuit.

bring: Past ECGs and echocardiograms, if you have them
steps: You undress to the waist and lie on your left side
ECG pads are stuck on your chest
Gel is put on, and a probe is placed on your chest in different spots
Sometimes you are asked to hold your breath
feel: The probe presses on your chest. It is a bit uncomfortable, but not painful
You may hear the sound of blood flow. This is normal
after: The report is usually ready right away or the same day

faq.q: How is an echo different from an ECG?
faq.a: An ECG records your heart's electrical activity. An echo shows its structure and movement.
